clue.text: Brief test without a problem's ending

parts.note: ex means without, as in ex dividend

indicators.note: the ending of a word is its final letter, taken here from problem

explanation.surface: A short quiz that came off without a hitch at the end.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is 'Brief test' because EXAM is short for examination.
explanation.definitionFit: Exam is the everyday shortened form of examination, a written or oral test.

clue.text: Desk one found in rectories all over the place

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.walkthrough: 'all over the place' turns RECTORIES into ESCRTOIRE, and 'found in' puts I inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a writing desk or bureau with drawers and pigeonholes.

clue.text: Sort of island, say, seen from south

clue.text: Sound judge of who's got the best hand

definitions.text: Sound judge of who's got the best hand

parts.words: Sound judge of who's got the best hand
parts.note: a device that measures how loud the clapping is, deciding which act earned the biggest round of applause, not a card game

explanation.surface: Someone rates which card player holds the strongest hand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hand' suggests cards, but a 'big hand' is applause; the judge is a gadget measuring sound in a talent contest.
explanation.definitionFit: This meter gauges the volume of applause, so it literally judges by sound who got the biggest hand.

clue.text: Playboy disappears in city on island

explanation.surface: A playboy vanishes in a city on an island.
explanation.walkthrough: The pieces simply run in order: 'in' and 'on' only join them.
explanation.definitionFit: A womaniser who is popular with women is a playboy, a phrase for a charmer.

clue.text: Show-off might, after change of heart

explanation.definitionFit: A poser is someone who poses for effect, a show-off.

explanation.definitionFit: Something with good and bad sides is a phrase for a benefit with drawbacks.

clue.text: Couple of points covered by characteristic passage

explanation.definitionFit: Transit is passage from one place to another.

clue.text: Gospel, but not the first book

parts.note: gospel means absolute truth, as in taking something as gospel

explanation.surface: A gospel that is not the first book of the Bible.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gospel' suggests Matthew, but it means truth; the answer is an Old Testament book.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a book of the Old Testament, named after a Moabite woman.

clue.text: Beetle, sort of vehicle to put an offer on

taken as written

clue.text: I'll tell you where sailors are surviving after onset of storm

definitions.text: I'll tell you where sailors are

indicators.note: after puts the word for surviving behind the storm's first letter
the onset of a word is its first letter, here taken from storm

parts.note: extant means still in existence, surviving

explanation.surface: A sailor reports where the crew are, still alive after a storm breaks.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a cryptic description: a navigational instrument that fixes a ship's position.
explanation.definitionFit: A navigational instrument measuring the sun's angle lets mariners fix their position at sea.

clue.text: Offender executed by governor taking trips round British Islands

parts.note: a sinner is an offender against moral law
HE stands for His Excellency, the title of a governor
trips taken round, as on a fairground, are rides

explanation.surface: A colonial governor travels around with a condemned criminal in tow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Executed' means beheaded: the first letter goes. These are the Scottish island group off the west coast, nearer the mainland than the Outer Hebrides.
explanation.definitionFit: This archipelago off western Scotland includes Skye, Mull and Islay, a group of islands.

explanation.definitionFit: Overt describes something open and not hidden, so it is obvious and visible to anyone.

clue.text: Engineer lost item — equipment originally in plant

originally points to the first letter of equipment

explanation.surface: An engineer misplaces a part of the equipment while installed in a factory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plant' looks like a factory but is the definition: a parasitic shrub hung up at Christmas.
explanation.definitionFit: This evergreen parasitic shrub grows on trees and is a familiar Christmas plant.

clue.text: Catch this with harpoon?

parts.note: read as an instruction for a fishing method, it describes a fish whose name suggests the weapon used to land it

explanation.surface: A question about what sort of creature one would hunt with a harpoon.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a fish like a marlin, its name suggesting the spear used to catch fish.

clue.text: Use telephone receiver to earmark funds

parts.note: to ring someone is to call them on the telephone
a fence is a receiver of stolen goods

explanation.walkthrough: 'Receiver' looks like a phone handset, but it is a criminal dealer in stolen goods.
explanation.definitionFit: To protect money for one purpose only is the idiom of fencing it off, reserving funds.

clue.text: Opening of trunk from which one gets trumpets

parts.note: the trunk is an elephant's nose, and its opening is where the trumpeting sound comes out

explanation.walkthrough: 'Trunk' suggests a chest and 'trumpets' instruments; it is an elephant's nose and its call.

clue.text: Oddly shown, witch flying at 743 mph!

explanation.definitionFit: The adjective relates to the speed of sound, roughly 743 miles per hour at sea level.

clue.text: Not used to numbers entering prison?

explanation.walkthrough: 'overthrowing' turns AIDNI round as a whole. NI is Northern Ireland, which Britons call the Province.

newspapers, the Daily Telegraph and Sunday Telegraph among them

clue.text: Travel with purpose
